title: GPU Reservation Contingency Matrix + Exchange Rules — 2029-03
abstract: Working spreadsheet to define contingency exchange rules, credit transfer mechanics, and operational triggers for dedicated GPU reservations across regions and customer contracts. Focus on fair exchange ratios, cooldowns, priority arbitration and minimal SLA impact in shortfalls.
assumptions: All reserved capacity values are in v100-equivalent GPU units (quarterly normalized).
Cross-region transfer is allowed only when customer contract explicitly permits exchange or when emergency pool activated.
Burst buffer equals 10% of an active contract's baseline unless overridden by contract terms.
Reserved SLA tiers: Gold (99.95 latency uptime), Silver (99.5), Bronze (best-effort).
Exchange penalties are billed monthly as credit adjustments, not immediate refunds.

exchange_rule_summary: Default exchange ratio = min(borrower_priority_factor, lender_flexibility_factor) * 0.8 where factors are computed from tier and contract term length.
Cooldown enforced after exchange to avoid oscillation: default 48 hours (configurable per contract).
Emergency pool activation requires SRE and sales sign-off; emergency pool drains into borrower as 1:1 credits but with 20% replenishment fee applied to lender's next invoice.
Cross-region exchanges add a latency-risk surcharge: 5-15% additional credit cost based on measured RTT delta; applied to borrower monthly reconciliation.
operational_runbook_steps: 1) Detect shortfall: Automated alert when sustained 75%+ utilization on reserved slab for 4+ hours.
2) Auto-evaluate candidates: Allocation engine ranks potential lenders by flexibility and proximity. If score > 0.7, propose auto-borrow.
3) Notify stakeholders: Send Slack thread to #sre-capacity and notify Customer Success + contract owner with proposed exchange and expected impact window.
4) Execute exchange: If auto-borrow enabled by contract, allocation engine executes transfer and marks lender cooldown. Otherwise queue human approval.
5) Telemetry tagging: All borrowed tokens tagged with origin-contract, exchange-ratio, and TTL for chargeback reconciliation.
6) Reversion: At TTL expiry or when utilization normalizes (<60% for 12h), system rebalances back to original owners respecting cooldowns.
7) Post-incident reconciliation: Run billing adj script and append to monthly contract reconciliation report.
decision_points: Threshold for auto-borrow from emergency-pool: sustained 90% utilization for 3h AND absence of available regional lenders.
When to preempt Silver/Bronze from dedicated-slab: only after human review if Gold customers would otherwise violate 99.95 SLA.
Penalty waiver clause: waive 50% of replenishment fee if customers agree to scheduled maintenance window within 72h.
Escalation path: SRE on-call -> Capacity PM -> Head of Infra -> Legal for cross-contract disputes.
metrics_targets: Target reserved utilization (global): 72% avg per week (goal to reduce waste while maintaining headroom)
Regional buffer target: 12% of active reserved capacity
Emergency pool size: 2% of global reserved fleet but not less than 16 GPUs
Max borrow duration: 14 days for non-emergency exchanges
Rebalance success rate target: 98% automated reversion without human intervention
billing_and_accounting_notes: All exchanges recorded as credit movements in monthly invoice; show lender credit applied as negative line item and borrower surcharge as separate line item.
Replenishment fee defaults to 20% of borrowed-credit value unless overridden by contract addendum.
Audit trail must include allocation IDs, timestamps, exchange ratio calc, and approver IDs for any manual actions.
open_questions: Should we support partial-GPU fractional exchanges for pods using multi-tenant inferencing? (engineering impact significant)
How to model network egress and warmed KV-cache costs into cross-region exchange pricing?
Do sales agreements need a clear stockout SLA addendum to enable automated exchanges without manual approvals?
recent_changes_and_review_notes: 2029-02-10: tightened cooldown from 72->48 hours based on oscillation tests (Marcus)
